articles.title: Como escolher um aspirador-robô para a sua casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Guia mostra o que avaliar antes da compra, como bateria, sensores, função de passar pano, app e tipo de limpeza para cada tamanho de casa.
articles.summary: Dos modelos básicos aos mais avançados, entenda quais funções realmente fazem diferença na limpeza, na autonomia e no uso com pets e tapetes.
articles.body:
Positivo PRA2000 voltando para a base de esvaziamento — Foto: Henrique Martin/g1

Existem muitos modelos diferentes de aspiradores-robô no mercado, cada qual com seu nível de complexidade, recursos e independência.

Um aspirador-robô pode fazer apenas uma aspiração rápida em um apartamento pequeno ou uma limpeza completa com pano úmido em uma casa grande.

Para entender qual é o modelo que atende às suas necessidades, o Guia de Compras separou 10 questões sobre o aspirador-robô para ajudar com as principais dúvidas relacionadas ao produto.

O aparelho limpa pisos frios, de madeira e a maioria dos tapetes. Ele anda sozinho pelo ambiente, tocando em paredes ou usando sensores para detectar a proximidade de objetos e mudar de direção. Também aspira pelos de pets, cabelos e farelos.

No entanto, ele não limpa cantos de paredes perfeitamente, já que as escovas giratórias nem sempre conseguem alcançar as quinas.

O robô também não substitui a faxina feita com um aspirador de maior porte ou panos com produtos de limpeza. No geral, o eletrodoméstico é feito para manter a casa limpa, e não para fazer uma limpeza pesada do zero.

Com sistemas de mapeamento e navegação: São os aspiradores-robô mais avançados e caros, mas é a categoria mais recomendada para compra pelo número de funções disponíveis e a queda no preço nos últimos anos.

Além do giroscópio, usam câmeras integradas e sensores a laser para criar um mapa da casa e detectar objetos no caminho.

Sensores na base identificam o tipo de piso e ajustam a potência da limpeza. Aplicativos para celular permitem acompanhar o consumo de energia e criar um mapa de limpeza personalizado.

Os modelos mais avançados podem ter uma base de carregamento com um saco acoplado, que esvazia o reservatório do aspirador após cada faxina. E os mais avançados ainda contam com um depósito de água para limpar o piso e remover os resíduos de forma automática.

Básicos: Seguem um programa de limpeza automático que varre e aspira o ambiente. Também podem passar pano seco.

Não fazem mapeamento do ambiente nem podem ser programados para funções independentes. Precisam ser carregados na tomada manualmente. Desconfie se o produto custa menos de R$ 200, pois existem relatos de aparelhos baratos que não têm poder de sucção suficiente.

Programáveis: Podem ser controlados por controle remoto ou aplicativo de celular. Oferecem mais modos de limpeza, como automática, aleatória, bordas e zigue-zague. Podem passar pano seco ou úmido.

Costumam ter giroscópio para facilitar a navegação e evitar batidas desnecessárias. Vêm com base de carregamento e voltam sozinhos para recarregar.

O equipamento usa escovas giratórias nas extremidades que empurram a sujeira para o meio do aparelho , onde fica uma escova central. De lá, a sujeira vai para o reservatório de poeira.

Quanto maior o reservatório, maior a quantidade de faxinas que o produto consegue realizar sem precisar ser esvaziado.

O aspirador-robô pode trabalhar sozinho, sem supervisão. Isso é muito mais fácil com aparelhos mais caros, que mapeiam o ambiente.

Sem o mapeamento, a maioria pode se deparar com pontos apertados, como vãos entre móveis ou pernas de mesas, de onde não conseguirá sair sem bater bastante. Isso significa demora na limpeza e maior consumo da bateria.

Depende do produto. No geral, a duração estimada pelos fabricantes vai de 30 minutos a mais de duas horas, dependendo do modelo e das condições de uso.

Alguns vêm com base de carregamento e conseguem retornar a ela sozinhos, podendo interromper a faxina no meio para recarregar e só depois terminar a limpeza.

🪜 O aspirador-robô sobe degraus? Ele pode cair?

As rodinhas do aspirador-robô são emborrachadas para não marcarem o piso e ajudam o equipamento a subir em pequenas superfícies, como a borda de um tapete.

Se o obstáculo for mais alto que poucos centímetros, ele não vai subir. Além disso, grande parte dos modelos conta com um sensor antiquedas, que evita acidentes em degraus ou escadas.

No exterior, já existem aspiradores-robô com uma espécie de suporte que ajuda a subir pequenos degraus. E até um com uma garra que pega meias e pequenos objetos no meio do caminho e leva para um local seguro.

As versões mais simples passam somente um pano seco de microfibra, que fica encaixado embaixo do aspirador.

Modelos intermediários e avançados usam um reservatório de água, que libera o líquido no pano conforme a limpeza ocorre.

Os fabricantes ressaltam que o reservatório deve ser preenchido apenas com água, sem produtos de limpeza, para evitar danos ao aparelho.

Apesar disso, a função de passar pano é apenas um complemento. Como o aspirador-robô é muito leve, ele não consegue fazer pressão sobre o piso para uma limpeza mais profunda.

🛏️ O aspirador-robô entra debaixo dos móveis?

Na média, os aspiradores-robô têm entre 7,5 cm e 10 cm de altura. É importante verificar o espaço embaixo dos móveis de casa, como sofás e camas, e comparar com o modelo escolhido para saber se o aparelho não vai entalar.

Sim, mas pode ser preciso passar por um período de adaptação. Cães e gatos podem se assustar ou atacar o equipamento. Por conta disso, é bom supervisionar os pets no início do uso.

Caso seu bichinho faça necessidades fora do lugar, o robô pode criar um rastro de sujeira pela casa toda se estiver programado para limpar o ambiente sozinho.

Nesse caso, é mais recomendável optar por um modelo mais caro que tenha sensores de objetos no caminho, capazes de desviar da sujeira.

O reservatório de poeira precisa ser limpo sempre que estiver cheio. A exceção são os modelos que contam com uma torre de esvaziamento autônomo. É como se o aspirador tivesse seu próprio limpador.

Na hora da compra, verifique também se o fabricante oferece peças extras para reposição, como escovas, rodas e filtros, que se desgastam com o uso. Avalie ainda se a marca conta com assistência técnica local em caso de problemas.

O aspirador-robô já vem programado para fazer uma limpeza padrão ao ser ligado. Em geral, ele aspira o meio do ambiente, depois os cantos e termina em espiral. Nos equipamentos mais simples, isso é tudo o que eles podem fazer, sem personalização.

Modelos mais eficientes vêm com controle remoto ou permitem comandos via aplicativo no celular, nas versões com wi-fi integrado. Neles, você pode programar se quer aspirar ou passar pano, escolher a intensidade de sucção e até optar por limpar apenas um quarto da casa.

Nos aspiradores mais caros, o aparelho ajusta sozinho a potência de sucção ao verificar o nível de sujeira. Eles também podem indicar se os acessórios precisam ser substituídos.

Veja a seguir uma lista de seis modelos mais avançados de aspiradores-robô. Eles custavam entre R$ 2.200 e R$ 6.000 nas lojas on-line consultadas em setembro.

articles.title: Firing at Punjab home of singer who was close to Sidhu Moosewala
articles.summary: Masked men fired 6-7 shots at Punjabi singer Gulab Sidhu’s Barnala home gate; no injuries. Police recovered shells, filed attempt-to-murder, Arms Act case.
articles.body: BATHINDA: Three masked assailants fired at least six shots at the home of Punjabi singer Gulab Sidhu in Pharwahi village, Barnala district, early Sunday. No injuries were reported.CCTV footage captured the attack at 1:33 am. The bullets hit the home’s iron gate, according to residents. Police recovered six empty shells from the site.Sidhu was not home during the incident, as he is currently abroad promoting his film ‘Judaa‘, released Aug 21. A song from the film has drawn 7.4 million views onlineBarnala senior superintendent of police (SSP) Mohammad Sarfaraz Alam said a case of attempt to murder and under Arms Act has been registered against unidentified suspects. Alam said Sidhu had faced threats earlier. He had been assigned two gunmen.Sidhu was close to slain rapper Shubhdeep Singh, known as Sidhu Moose Wala, and displays “Justice for Sidhu Moosewala“ on his Instagram profile.An unverified audio clip posted on social media in the name of gangster Dony Bal claimed responsibility for the attack. The speaker alleged Sidhu used Moose Wala’s name while performing for Moose Wala’s rivals. articles.title: ‘CM Vijay’  WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh
articles.summary: Bengaluru security guard lost Rs 1.04 lakh after a WhatsApp deepfake video call posing as “CM Vijay” promised Rs 11 lakh aid and demanded fees; case filed.
articles.body: BENGALURU: “I am CM Vijay. I am here to help you,” a voice and face appearing on a WhatsApp video call allegedly convinced a 29-year-old security guard that he was speaking to Tamil Nadu chief minister and actor C Joseph Vijay.Promised Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, the unsuspecting man ended up losing over Rs 1 lakh after a fraudster allegedly used a deepfake AI-generated video and repeatedly demanded processing fees and other payments. This is the first such case reported in the city.According to the complaint filed by Ratikanta Giri, a native of Odisha who has been working in the city for the last 20 years, he received a WhatsApp video call from the number 7986304658 on Sept 9. Soon after he answered the call, he saw Tamil Nadu CM “Vijay” introducing himself. The fraudster claimed he was providing financial aid to people facing economic hardship.“After introducing himself as CM Vijay in Hindi, I was asked about my name, profession and where I stay. After answering the questions, I was offered financial help from Vijay’s personal account,” he told TOI.“I refused any help, but the person on the video call repeatedly asked me to accept it, saying that he was helping many people. He then told me that his manager would contact me and that the funds would be transferred by him. He asked me to follow the instructions of his manager,” Giri said.The manager offered Rs 11 lakh in aid, claiming that the money would be transferred to Giri’s account through Vijay’s foreign account in dollars. Later, the ‘manager’ told him that Rs 5 lakh had been immediately allotted to him.Initially, Giri was asked to pay Rs 5,000 as exchange charges. Later, he was told that his PIN number had been locked and that he needed to pay Rs 18,000 to release it. When Giri refused, he was allegedly told that he would lose his earlier payment of Rs 5,000.Giri said, “I initially paid Rs 18,000. Later, another person claiming to be Thakur from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) contacted me and demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine imposed by the agency. Fearing I would lose my earlier payments, I transferred the money. I made a few more payments totalling over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app. When the fraudsters demanded another Rs 50,000, I refused and realised I had been duped.”Giri later contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 before approaching Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act.To convince him to make the payments, the fraudsters sent Giri a letter claiming that Rs 5 lakh had been allotted to him. They also shared identity proof purportedly belonging to a CBI officer.“We urge people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims,” a senior officer said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Air Force officer prayed while "free-falling" after being shot down in Iran
articles.summary: Badly wounded and alone in Iran's desert, downed U.S. Air Force officer Dude 44 Bravo evaded capture for days as the Iranian forces and the U.S. military sea...
articles.body:
The Air Force colonel needed help when he crashed over a mountainous part of Iran's desert, separated from his crewmate, the pilot of the F-15E, after being shot down by Iran in April.

The U.S. aviator free-fell to the ground at an estimated 70-100 mph; the Iranian shoulder-fired missile had damaged his parachute. He was the backseater, the weapons-systems officer on a two-man crew with the mission call sign Dude 44. The pilot was Alpha; he was Bravo.

"At one point when I looked up and saw no parachute, that was the most terrifying thing I've ever seen," Bravo said in his first public account of what happened. "So I paused, right then, and I prayed, 'Lord, your will be done. But if I'm getting through this, I need help.'"

Help took two days to come. Bravo, who broke his back, an arm and a shoulder after hitting the ground at such high speed, hid and survived two days behind enemy lines before his rescue . He calls it a "modern-day miracle."

"I believe that it's a testament to God's provision in my life to bring me through that moment in a way that didn't prevent injuries, but prevented any catastrophic injuries that would have affected my ability to survive," Bravo, identified by his mission call sign due to security threats, said.

Dude 44's mission in Iran, and what went wrong

The U.S. military has flown around 13,000 missions so far in the war with Iran , according to Adm. Brad Cooper, the American commander of U.S. Central Command leading U.S. forces in the Middle East. Dude 44's mission the night of April 2 was near a mountainous area south of the city of Isfahan, close to where Iran had been keeping much of its highly enriched nuclear material . According to Cooper, Dude 44's mission that night was to conduct a strike on industrial facilities related to Iran's drone and missile program.

"We had air superiority, but clearly we weren't flying over Kansas," Cooper said.

The $30 million two-seat F-15E, a workhorse of American air combat operations for decades, was brought down by a shoulder-fired missile, which can cost around $100,000.

"That day was just another day in the war for us, until the moment where we got hit by an Iranian weapon," Bravo said.

When the missile hit, a moment Bravo describes as "getting hit by a freight train," Bravo said he and Alpha did everything they could to try to save the fighter jet. It quickly became clear the plane couldn't be saved, so the pair ejected.

Alpha, who ejected safely and was rescued before Bravo, is already back flying for the Air Force. He declined 60 Minutes' request for an interview due to security considerations. Alpha expressed his gratitude for the rescue of both himself and Bravo in a statement provided to 60 Minutes.

"I am still in awe of the professionalism and tactical prowess of the Combat Search and Rescue specialists and the Joint Force who executed the rescue missions of me and DUDE 44 Bravo, both those in theater and behind the scenes," Alpha said in a statement. "Words cannot capture how thankful my family and I are and how proud I am to serve alongside each and every one of them."

60 Minutes learned that Bravo landed hard, about 5 miles away from Alpha after struggling with his damaged parachute.

"I had injuries, but we all train to adapt and overcome the things that we're faced with," he said. "I moved as quickly as I could, despite the injuries, away from the place that I landed."

It was dark out, but Bravo said he began to be able to discern some of his surroundings as the sun came up, like being on an early morning hunting trip.

"And in the heart of Iran, where we were, there are high desert valleys, but also amazing craggly cliffs. And so I find myself in one of those valleys with cliffs on either side," Bravo said.

He realized the safest place to go was up and, despite his broken bones, hiked and climbed up a 7,000-foot ridgeline.

"Never let a lack of motivation put you on Iranian TV," Bravo said.

Back in the United States, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was woken in the middle of the night with the news. He said he immediately jumped to the next steps: asking if the crew was OK, and whether Iran knew what had happened.

"Whether they're alive or not, we're going to go get them," he said.

Evidence of the wreckage was shared by Iranian media, and videos emerged online of armed groups hunting for the downed crew. According to U.S. military sources, Iranians got to within a few hundred meters of Bravo.

"There was clear intent out of the Iranian ground force to come find those two guys," Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and a former fighter pilot himself, said.

During the "race against time," the U.S. military closely tracked Iranians in the area, Cooper said.

One of the most complex rescue operations in U.S. military history

Six hours in, the U.S. was able to rescue Alpha in a risky daytime raid. American helicopters in the rescue force took fire.

"It was a gun fight all the way in and all the way out," Hegseth said. "But they got Alpha back."

The job was only half done. Alpha's rescue force was unable to find Bravo and withdrew.

But as night fell on that first day in Iran, Bravo was able to send a message back home.

"When I got to the moment where I could review and think about all that I'd gone through, I sent, 'God is good,' as a recognition of all that he had brought me through," Bravo said.

He also alerted the U.S. military he'd been hurt, but that he was moving. A rescue force was almost sent in not long after, but Hegseth said "it just didn't line up."

"That was a really tough decision," he said. "I'll never forget, you know, being in the situation room and saying, 'OK, I guess we're gonna roll 24,' which means, 'Hey, Bravo's going to be out there for basically 24 hours more.'"

Bravo survived with almost no water or food, in the wind and cold of the high mountain desert, for another full day.

The CIA played a pivotal role in Bravo's rescue. The agency launched a multi-pronged deception campaign to confuse Iranian forces looking for Bravo. It also used top-secret technology to pinpoint Bravo's location.

To clear the way for Bravo's rescue, newly declassified video shows American bombers and drones hit Iran's Revolutionary Guard forces nearby where he was hiding. Then it was time to go back in for Bravo.

There were over 90 U.S. service members on the ground — the first U.S. boots on the ground in Iran in 46 years, Adm. Cooper said. Several hundred people were in the air, and several thousand served as support in the rescue mission.

"I think what you need to know is we would have sent more to go get the back-seater," Gen. Caine said, referring to Bravo's position in the fighter jet.

The force came in on two large search-and-rescue planes and landed on a makeshift desert airstrip. Then they launched small "Little Bird" helicopters capable of reaching Bravo on the ridgeline, several miles away.

"One of the greatest moments of my life"

Bravo said it was "one of the greatest moments of my life" when he saw his rescuers. While Bravo doesn't want to share the exact details of his conversation with them, he did share what he said when they first got to him.

But Bravo and the others on the ground were not yet out of danger. The rescue planes' landing gear was stuck in the desert sand of the makeshift airstrip. The planes could not take off, and more than 90 of what Admiral Cooper described as the military's "most elite service members" were stuck until a clandestine Air Force unit came to the rescue.

The U.S. destroyed the two marooned aircraft, worth about $100 million each, as well as the Little Bird helicopters, so the technology wouldn't fall into Iranian hands.

Fifty hours after being shot down, Bravo was safe, rescued as the sun rose on Easter Sunday. Not long after leaving Iran, Bravo called his wife back home in the U.S.

"I was really proud of her and grateful for the strength that she showed," Bravo said.

The officer says he wants the American people to know that the rescue is about more than what he went through.

"It's a story of the teamwork, the training, of the faith, of the decisions and the leadership to do something that will live in history as an example of what America's willing to do, in order to uphold our promise and leave no man behind."

articles.title: TRE manda Raquel Lyra apagar vídeo com falso direito de resposta | G1
articles.standfirst: Desembargador eleitoral também determinou que o conteúdo seja removido de sites e plataformas que o publicaram, sob multa diária de R$ 15 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: Desembargador eleitoral também determinou que o conteúdo seja removido de sites e plataformas que o publicaram, sob multa diária de R$ 15 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
Raquel Lyra (PSD) e João Campos (PSB) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A Justiça Eleitoral mandou tirar do ar um vídeo da campanha da governadora e candidata à reeleição Raquel Lyra ( PSD ), incluindo suas republicações em redes sociais e sites, pelo uso de forma indevida da expressão “Direito de Resposta”, sem obter vitória judicial contra o adversário João Campos ( PSB ). O material também aparentou usar voz gerada por inteligência artificial sem o aviso obrigatório aos eleitores, segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Pernambuco (TRE).

“Ao estampar a expressão ‘Direito de Resposta’ em sua publicidade, a campanha representada pratica ato de gravíssima desinformação institucional, que afronta não apenas o adversário, mas a própria Justiça Eleitoral. [...] Trata-se da apropriação indevida de um instituto jurídico-processual no intuito de simular uma chancela inexistente do Poder Judiciário", afirmou o desembargador Paulo Augusto de Freitas Oliveira na determinação judicial.

A Justiça foi acionada pela coligação Frente Popular de Pernambuco, que representa João Campos. Cabe recurso à decisão liminar, deferida no domingo (13), mas o vídeo foi apagado do perfil de Raquel Lyra no Instagram dentro do prazo de 24 horas que foi concedido pelo desembargador. O magistrado determinou a suspensão do anúncio pago na Meta, a remoção de postagens no Instagram, TikTok, Facebook e YouTube, além de publicações nos sites que republicaram o vídeo.

"A manutenção de uma propaganda irregular de caráter negativo, desprovida de transparência técnica (IA) e ancorada em premissa oficial falsa gera contínuo desequilíbrio na disputa eleitoral, possuindo potencial lesivo irreparável à lisura do pleito à medida que atinge milhares de eleitores a cada instante”, declarou o desembargador na decisão.

Em caso de descumprimento, a multa é de R$ 15 mil por dia para plataformas e sites ou para quem fizer novas republicações ou compartilhamentos do vídeo. Além disso, a Justiça ordenou ao Facebook que informe, em 48 horas, dados como valor gasto, origem e meio de pagamento, sobre o contratante, alcance, número de impressões, como o anúncio foi segmentado e se houve declaração do uso de IA.

João Campos se pronunciou, numa postagem no X , sobre a decisão judicial. "A Justiça Eleitoral acaba de confirmar: a verdade está do nosso lado. Não adianta tentar confundir as pessoas com 'direito de resposta' fake só porque cobramos explicações sobre o supersalário. Vamos em frente, com respeito e trabalho de verdade pelo futuro de Pernambuco", postou o ex-prefeito do Recife .

O g1 entrou em contato com a assessoria da coligação Pernambuco de Coração, que representa Raquel Lyra, para obter uma resposta sobre essa decisão judicial, mas não recebeu retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na determinação judicial, o desembargador argumentou que:

O impulsionamento pago não pode ser usado para atacar adversário: a Justiça considerou que o conteúdo do vídeo não apenas defendia a candidata, mas também fazia ataque direto ao adversário, ao chamá-lo de “desesperado”, “imaturo”, “despreparado”, além de dizer ao eleitor para “não apostar nessa aventura”;

Houve uso da expressão “Direito de Resposta” sem decisão judicial que autorizasse isso: segundo o TRE, o vídeo passava aos eleitores a ideia de que a Justiça Eleitoral teria reconhecido formalmente um direito de resposta da campanha de Raquel Lyra, mas isso não ocorreu, pois a análise da solicitação foi adiada;

O vídeo aparenta usar voz sintética sem o aviso obrigatório: o magistrado considerou que o conteúdo, em exame preliminar, aparenta ser narrado por voz gerada por IA, sem a sinalização exigida pela norma eleitoral;

Há risco de dano pela velocidade de circulação do conteúdo: de acordo com a decisão judicial, o vídeo estava circulando no ambiente digital com rapidez e havia relato de alcance superior a 1 milhão de usuários apenas no formato pago.

Ainda na decisão, o magistrado determinou que:

os representados, após serem notificados da decisão, têm até dois dias para apresentar defesa;

depois, o Ministério Público Eleitoral será intimado a se manifestar em um dia;

em seguida, o processo volta ao TRE para nova análise.

articles.title: Após quatro anos afastada dos palcos, Simaria se declara para fãs | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista pausou agenda de shows após fim da dupla 'Simone e Simaria', em 2022. primeiro show de carreira solo da baiana aconteceu em São Paulo.
articles.summary: Artista pausou agenda de shows após fim da dupla 'Simone e Simaria', em 2022. primeiro show de carreira solo da baiana aconteceu em São Paulo.
articles.body:
Simaria em show de retorno em São Paulo — Foto: Redes sociais

Após quatro anos afastada dos palcos, a cantora Simaria se declarou para os fãs no show de retorno, no sábado (12), em São Paulo. Nas redes sociais, a artista compartilhou fotos e vídeos da apresentação.

"Eu tentei imaginar esse momento muitas vezes. Nenhuma delas chegou perto do que vocês me fizeram sentir na noite de ontem. Obrigada por esperarem, por cantarem e por viverem essa noite comigo", escreveu.

O show em São Paulo também marcou a gravação do primeiro DVD da carreira solo do artista. A data de lançamento ainda não foi divulgada.

Ao anunciar o show, em agosto desse ano, Simaria já havia reforçado que a pausa na carreira foi necessária para a sua saúde mental.

“A pausa nunca foi o fim da minha história. Foi só o tempo que eu precisei para voltar bem! E meu reencontro com a música tem data e lugar para acontecer”, disse.

Simaria estava afastada dos palcos desde 2022, quando ela e Simone encerraram a carreira como dupla. Juntas, elas emplacaram diversos sucessos como “Loka”, “Meu Violão e o Nosso Cachorro” e “Regime Fechado”.

Após o fim, Simone seguiu carreira solo e se consolidou no sertanejo.

articles.title: Quem é o deputado federal Cezinha de Madureira, pastor evangélico alvo de operação da PF  | G1
articles.standfirst: Filiado ao PL de Jair Bolsonaro, ele é pastor da Assembleia de Deus – Ministério de Madureira, em São Paulo, ligado ao bispo Samuel Ferreira, uma das principais lideranças do ministério no estado.
articles.summary: Filiado ao PL de Jair Bolsonaro, ele é pastor da Assembleia de Deus – Ministério de Madureira, em São Paulo, ligado ao bispo Samuel Ferreira, uma das principais lideranças de SP.
articles.body:
Jornalista, radialista e pastor evangélico, Cezinha se filiou recentemente ao PL. Ele é pastor da Assembleia de Deus – Ministério de Madureira, em São Paulo, ligado ao bispo Samuel Ferreira, uma das principais lideranças do ministério no estado.

O deputado foi eleito para a Câmara dos Deputados em 2018 e reeleito em 2022 com 143.434 votos. Na época, ele estava no PSD de Gilberto Kassab e mudou para PL só depois da reeleição para deputado federal.

Antes, ele foi deputado estadual na Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo ( Alesp ) pelo mesmo PSD. Ao ser eleito deputado federal, ele se tornou um dos principais nomes da bancada evangélica no Congresso Nacional.

O deputado federal Antonio Cezar Correia Freire, o Cezinha de Madureira (PL-SP) é um influente parlamentar evangélico de São Paulo. Ele é pastor da Assembleia de Deus – Ministério de Madureira. — Foto: Divulgação/Câmara dos Deputados

Natural de Ipiaú, na Bahia, onde nasceu em 1973, ele se mudou para São Paulo em 1991 e trabalhou em diversas emissoras de rádio comunitárias e evangélicas.

Atualmente, ele apresenta o programa ‘Palavra de Vida’, na rádio Musical FM de SP, ao lado do bispo Samuel Ferreira, seu padrinho político e religioso.

O deputado federal Cezinha de Madureira (PL) em seus périplos ao lado do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Amigo pessoal do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), Cezinha era visto constantemente na garupa das motos do ex-presidente durante as chamadas 'motociatas', participando com ele inclusive de idas a jogos de futebol, na época que Jair ainda era presidente da República.

Cezinha também foi o principal cabo eleitoral do ministro André Mendonça para a vaga de ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ).

Na época da indicação de Mendonça para o cargo, o deputado percorreu os gabinetes dos senadores, pedindo voto favorável para o ex-advogado geral da União de Bolsonaro ser alçado ao cargo de ministro do STF.

Bolsonaro em encontro com o deputado federal da bancada evangélica Cezinha de Madureira e o indicado ao STF, André Mendonça, em 2021. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Apesar da ligação com o bolsonarista, em 16 de outubro de 2025 Cezinha esteve com o padrinho político no gabinete do presidente Lula ( PT ).

Na época da visita de Samuel Ferreira ao gabinete do presidente, Cezinha foi fotografado ao lado do também indicado de Lula ao STF, o advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias.

Messias também é evangélico e foi indicado ao STF pelo petista. Mas a indicação dele foi barrada em votação no plenário do Senado Federal , em derrota histórica para o governo Lula.

Durante a visita de 2025, Samuel Ferreira presenteou Lula com uma bíblia e orou com o presidente e o pupilo dentro do gabinete presidencial.

O bispo Samuel Ferreira e o deputado Cezinha de Madureira são recebidos pelo presidente Lula (PT) em outubro de 2025. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Queda de árvore bloqueia trecho da Avenida do Estado no acesso à Marginal Tietê | G1
articles.standfirst: Via está interditada entre a Avenida Santos Dumont e a Marginal Tietê; equipes trabalham na remoção da árvore e motoristas precisam utilizar rotas alternativas.
articles.summary: Via está interditada entre a Avenida Santos Dumont e a Marginal Tietê; equipes trabalham na remoção da árvore e motoristas precisam utilizar rotas alternativas.
articles.body:
Uma queda de árvore bloqueia a Avenida do Estado, na manhã desta segunda-feira (14), entre a Avenida Santos Dumont e a Marginal Tietê, no sentido da marginal, na região central de São Paulo.

Segundo a Secretaria Municipal das Subprefeituras (SMSUB), equipes trabalham na remoção da árvore e na limpeza da via, na altura do número 681, para liberar o trânsito.

Com a interdição, motoristas que vêm do Centro ou da região do Ipiranga e pretendem acessar a Marginal Tietê precisam buscar caminhos alternativos.

Quem segue em direção à Marginal pode continuar até a Ponte Cruzeiro do Sul, pela avenida de mesmo nome. Outra alternativa é acessar a Avenida Santos Dumont no sentido Santana.

Para quem pretende seguir no sentido da Rodovia Castello Branco, uma das opções é ir até a rotatória do Anhembi, acessar a Avenida Olavo Fontoura e, depois, entrar na Marginal Tietê.

O bloqueio também pode afetar linhas intermunicipais que atendem cidades como Guarulhos, Arujá e Santa Isabel. Ônibus que utilizam esse trecho fazem o retorno para seguir pela Avenida do Estado, no sentido Ipiranga, até o Terminal Metropolitano Armênia.

Artesp informa que 19 linhas do transporte intermunicipal de ônibus estão com atrasos, devido a interdição na Avenida do Estado por queda de árvore. São linhas que passam por lá e também saem ou chegam do Metrô Armênia

articles.title: Coletores de lixo em São José dos Campos fazem paralisação | G1
articles.standfirst: Funcionários de empresa terceirizada não saíram para a coleta nesta segunda-feira (14) e protestam em frente à empresa, no bairro Chácaras Reunidas.
articles.summary: Coletores de lixo em São José dos Campos protestam por reajuste salarial e melhorias no convênio médico, afetando o serviço nesta segunda-feira (14).
articles.body:
Coletores de lixo orgânico fazem paralisação em São José dos Campos — Foto: Andressa Lorenzetti/TV Vanguarda

Parte dos coletores de lixo orgânico de São José dos Campos fez uma paralisação na manhã desta segunda-feira (14) e não saiu para realizar a coleta. Os funcionários se reuniram em frente à empresa responsável pelo serviço, no bairro Chácaras Reunidas.

Segundo os trabalhadores, a paralisação ocorre por reivindicações trabalhistas. Entre os pedidos estão reajuste salarial, novos equipamentos de proteção individual (EPIs) e mudanças no convênio médico.

Os funcionários também reclamam da troca do plano de saúde, que, segundo eles, passou a oferecer menos opções de atendimento na região.

Os trabalhadores aguardam uma manifestação da empresa e afirmam que pretendem retomar as atividades após receber uma resposta.

Ao g1 , o Sindicato dos Trabalhadores em Empresas de Prestação de Serviços de Asseio e Conservação e Limpeza Urbana (Siemaco) informou que não participa da paralisação e considera o movimento ilegal.

Segundo a entidade, os funcionários decidiram interromper as atividades por conta própria, sem comunicar previamente o sindicato. O Siemaco afirmou ainda que a empresa cumpre a obrigação de oferecer convênio médico e que a reivindicação dos trabalhadores se refere à troca do plano, uma questão que, na avaliação da entidade, poderia ser resolvida por meio de negociação.

Até o momento, cerca de 30% dos funcionários aderiram à paralisação, segundo o sindicato, que também afirmou haver uso político do movimento por parte de alguns trabalhadores.

A empresa ainda não havia se manifestado.

articles.standfirst: Municípios estão no painel de alertas desde o início do fim de semana; região bragantina ainda enfrenta cheia de rios e há risco de deslizamentos em outras áreas.
articles.summary: Com solo encharcado, o alerta de chuva no Vale do Paraíba e região bragantina segue para nove cidades com risco de deslizamentos e cheia de rios monitorados pelo Cemaden.
articles.body:
Nove cidades do Vale e região bragantina seguem em alerta do Cemaden por causa da chuva — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Nove cidades do Vale do Paraíba, Litoral Norte e região bragantina começaram a semana no painel de alertas do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) por causa das condições provocadas pelas chuvas. Os municípios estão no mapa desde o início do fim de semana e seguem nesta segunda-feira (14).

Estão em alerta Atibaia, Bragança Paulista, Paraibuna, São José dos Campos, Campos do Jordão, Ubatuba, Caraguatatuba, Ilhabela e São Sebastião.

Na região bragantina, a preocupação ainda é com a cheia dos rios. Em outras áreas, o principal risco é de deslizamentos de terra em encostas.

Nas últimas 24 horas, os maiores volumes de chuva foram registrados no Litoral Norte. Apesar de a região não registrar mais grandes acumulados, o solo permanece muito encharcado, o que aumenta o risco de ocorrências.

A previsão é de continuidade das chuvas na região, e as condições do solo são monitoradas pelas equipes responsáveis.

articles.body:
O chefe da Inteligência chinesa alertou que a inteligência artificial representa uma ameaça à segurança nacional do país, pois potências estrangeiras poderiam usá-la para minar a ordem social.

➡️ No fim de semana, o debate público sobre IA esquentou depois que dois pesquisadores da Anthropic emitiram alertas de que o rápido avanço da tecnologia poderia levar à extinção da raça humana num futuro não muito distante. O presidenO presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, comparou, neste domingo (13), os críticos da inteligência artificial a "forças muito negativas" que estão levantando cenários que não vão acontecer, e disse que quer garantir que os EUA continuem sendo os líderes do setor.

"Estamos liderando em relação à China em IA. Somos o país mais sofisticado do mundo e, francamente, quero manter assim porque quem vencer na IA, vence tudo [...] Poderíamos colocar barreiras de proteção. Podemos fazer isso e aquilo. Mas acho que há muitas forças muito negativas que estão trazendo esse assunto à tona quando não deveriam, e estão levantando coisas que não vão acontecer", declarou Trump aos jornalistas em seu campo de golfe na Irlanda, ao ser questionado se a indústria de IA deveria desacelerar ou ser mais regulamentada.te dos EUA, Donald Trump, criticou os alertas e indicou que não quer perder a corrida da IA para a China .

Sem mencionar os EUA, o ministro da Segurança do Estado chinês, Chen Yixin, afirmou que "forças hostis" abusam de tecnologias generativas de IA para "fabricar rumores políticos e espalhar informações prejudiciais" .

"Elas (forças hostis) estão travando guerras de opinião pública e guerras cognitivas contra a China, ameaçando diretamente nossa segurança política, institucional e ideológica", afirmou.

O alerta surge em um momento em que o líder chinês, Xi Jinping, tem um encontro marcado com o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , em Washington neste mês, para uma reunião focada na governança e segurança da IA, em meio a crescentes apelos por controles mais rígidos sobre a tecnologia.

Líderes tecnológicos dos EUA também pediram uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board bans pigeon feeding, Tehri at shrines, tweaks order after uproar
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: As Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi today announced prohibition of the feeding of birds and distribution of food .
articles.body: SRINAGAR: As Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi today announced prohibition of the feeding of birds and distribution of food items within the premises of all Waqf shrines across Jammu and Kashmir, it has created uproar in the Valley with many describing the directive as unnecessary.Announcing the decision early Sunday Andrabi, who is senior BJP leader, said that devotees, visitors and others should strictly comply with the order. She said the restrictions were aimed at maintaining cleanliness, hygiene, sanctity and a peaceful environment at the shrines.According to her, feeding birds and distributing food items could attract stray animals, lead to unhygienic conditions and cause inconvenience or disturbance to devotees engaged in prayers and worship.J&K Waqf Board doesn’t come under the elected Jammu and Kashmir government. “I am asking people to not bring Tehri to any shrine and I am asking that there should be no bird feeding. And I am announcing a ban on both these things. People should cooperate,” she announced the directive while talking to the media.In Kashmir bird feeding and distributing traditional Kashmiri yellow rice called Tehri is centuries old tradition. Tehri is prepared with turmeric, salt and mustard oil or ghee and cooked in large quantities and then distributed to devotees, children and passersby at the shrines as an act of faith and charity and it holds immense cultural, emotional and spiritual significance. Political leaders are asking Andrabi to reconsider her decision.National Conference leader Salman Sagar described it as another bad and unfortunate decision of Waqf.” It is interference in a place with which people are emotionally and spiritually connected. They just want to destroy everything spiritual here. The Waqf Board should focus on infrastructure development, creating universities and hospitals providing clean washrooms and rest rooms around shrines, which she has not done.Only thing the BJP leader does is play politics as Waqf chairperson and play spiritual practices of people,” Sagar said. A PDP representative Arif Amin said Tehri and feeding pigeons are centuries-old Khanqah traditions. “Banning them in the name of cleanliness isn’t just about right or wrong, it’s about the hope and healing of people who have suffered,” he said. “You cannot clean a shrine by erasing its soul. Fiddling with faith is unacceptable,” he said.Many others, however, argued that pigeons are very aggressive and they multiply rapidly. “Wherever Pigeons flock and stay, other birds simply disappear. Eagles and kites used to keep pigeons in check but those birds have also completely disappeared. Pigeons are responsible for spreading many diseases including those related to the chest and lungs.”Others also reacted sharply forcing Andrabi to slightly change her verbal directions. “There is no blanket ban on pigeon feeding or Tehri distribution. There is no directive. It is my own request that it shouldn’t be done inside the shrine as it creates a huge problem for us with stray dogs entering into the shrines,” she said. “I myself believe in these traditions but there should be a proper way to feed birds and distribute rice and people should adhere to cleanliness norms,” Andrabi told the TOI.Stay updated with the latest Srinagar news. articles.title: Banned scavenging killed them; their families now wait years for Rs 30L relief
articles.summary: Arjun Chauhan (37) knows he should not be doing it. The contract worker from Panvel knows septic tanks and sewers are to be cleaned by machines, not p.
articles.body: Arjun Chauhan (37) knows he should not be doing it. The contract worker from Panvel knows septic tanks and sewers are to be cleaned by machines, not people. He knows protective gear is mandatory. But when the call comes, he climbs in, with no safety cover.Chauhan has been doing this for 15-20 years, taking work from contractors, buildings and housing societies. A contractor pays him Rs 700-1,000 a day; others Rs 1,500-2,000. "There are lakhs like me who do this. After all, I have to put food on the table for my family," he said.His story is the reality behind the ban on manual scavenging: people continue to enter septic tanks, and when they die, their families spend years waiting for the statutory Rs 30 lakh compensation.For Ratanlal Jaiswar (54), that wait began in Dec 2024, when his son Chandan (22) died cleaning a septic tank at a chawl in Uran. Chandan, along with Vikas Kisan Tak (33) who too died, had entered the tank to rescue another worker who had collapsed inside.An FIR lodged was against the contractor, a suction-truck owner and one of the homeowners-all of whom had employed them to clean the tank without safety equipment.Nearly two years later, Ratanlal paints vehicles for a living and is awaiting the money. He wants to leave Taloja and return to UP, where his family is, and use the money to get his four children married. "I don't know how long I have to wait. Work dries up during monsoon, and when I don't find work, I sit here and sleep," he said.Tak's family is struggling too. They say the police initially refused to lodge an FIR, while the suction-truck owner offered to take care of the deceased's child's education. However, the family maintained that it wasn't enough as Tak was the sole breadwinner. His widow Archana (22), his mother and his sister Muskan now do domestic work to pay the rent for their room in Asudgaon, Panvel. Tak, who used to work as a driver-cleaner on the suction truck as well as do septic tank cleaning work, was paid Rs 17,000 a month, mostly in cash."I want my five-year-old son to complete his education. He is now my only hope to get out of this situation," Archana said.The same cycle has played out in other parts of Mumbai.In Powai, Akshay Mandal (23) andFulchand Kumar Saw (29) died in Nov 2025 while cleaning a sewage plant. "He was running the house. He used to send money so we could buy food and celebrate festivals," his father Jaynarayan, who travels to Mumbai from Jharkhand each year for work, says. Mandal's family got Rs 10 lakh from the contractor on humanitarian grounds but is awaiting the statutory compensation.Manual cleaning of manholes, septic tanks, and sewers is banned in India. But National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data shows 332 sanitation workers died in 18 states and UTs during hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks between Jan 1, 2021 and June 30, 2026. Maharashtra had the highest number of deaths at 58. Data tabled in the House in July 2025 by the state showed zero deaths in Mumbai between 2021 and 2024; a figure disputed by activists. Centre too has maintained that a survey found no manual scavengers in India."They want to hide the reality of caste-based discrimination. They don't accept the situation of Dalits who do scavenging," said Milind Ranade of Maharashtra Municipal Kamgar Union. He said the deaths reflect an indifference that has allowed the practice to persist. "The attitude remains: They are born to serve. Mar rahe hain, marne do."In the case of Jaiswar and Tak, the state said that since a private contractor engaged them, the compensation must be recovered from the employer. Bombay high court, however, held in Aug that the state must pay even when workers are privately engaged, and can recover it later from employers. It struck down Item 11 of 2019 and 2025 GRs, which forced private societies or contractors to pay instead of the state.Meanwhile, some families are awaiting enhanced compensation after Supreme Court, in 2023, raised it to Rs 30 lakh and directed govts to provide rehabilitation, including employment for next of kin and education for children.Nearly seven years after three workers died cleaning a tank in Govandi in 2019, each widow received Rs 10 lakh, but the balance has been pending. "It should've been released automatically. We have been trying to reach the authority, but there is no response. The approach remains casual," said advocate Abha Singh, who is pursuing the cases pro bono.Bezwada Wilson, national convenor of Safai Karmachari Andolan, says the delays show larger failure: "The govt has yet to acknowledge the extent to which manual scavenging continues, let alone identify those still trapped in it."But for those still doing the work, the distinction between what is legal and what happens on the ground is less important than the next day's wages. articles.summary: Europe News: Passengers screamed as severe turbulence jolted a Turkish Airlines flight from Istanbul to Tunisia during its descent on Thursday, with one traveller .
articles.body: Passengers screamed as severe turbulence jolted a Turkish Airlines flight from Istanbul to Tunisia during its descent on Thursday, with one traveller saying the aircraft “started to plummet” after three attempts to land in stormy conditions.The flight was approaching Tunis-Carthage International Airport when bad weather disrupted the landing. The aircraft was eventually diverted to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport, around 60 miles south of Tunis.Passenger Marina Maiskaya shared a video of the incident on Instagram, showing passengers gripping their seats as the aircraft shook and screams could be heard throughout the cabin.“The flight itself was smooth, but things turned absolutely terrifying as soon as we began our descent,” she wrote.“I have never in my life feared for my life like that, and my mom was with me, too.”Maiskaya said the pilot made three attempts to land at Tunis-Carthage International Airport while flying through the storm.“The pilot tried to land the plane at the same airport three times, flying right through a storm! We were shaken violently each time, and on the third attempt, we actually started to plummet,” she wrote.Passengers could be heard screaming as the aircraft appeared to suddenly lose altitude. “Here we started to fall down for a few seconds like free falling,” she said in the video.However, TOI could not independently verify the video. articles.title: Houthi drone attack: Saudi oil stocks could run dry within days if key pipeline remains shut
articles.summary: Middle East News: Saudi Arabia could run out of oil stocks for export within days if it fails to restart a major pipeline hit by drone attacks. The damage also threaten.
articles.body: Saudi Arabia could run out of oil stocks for export within days if it fails to restart a major pipeline hit by drone attacks. The damage also threatens to remove up to 4% of global oil supply from the market, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.The kingdom has enough crude at the Red Sea port of Yanbu to maintain exports for only five to seven days, news agency Reuters reported, citing three industry sources familiar with Saudi shipments. The stocks could eventually run out if the pipeline remains offline.The east-west pipeline was shut on Friday after drone attacks damaged the route. It carries Saudi crude from the country's oil fields in the east to Yanbu on the Red Sea.Saudi Arabia has not said how badly the pipeline was damaged or when it could restart.The timeline of the report could vary, according to the sources cited in the report. While one stated the repairs could take five to six weeks, another said the pipeline could be repaired sooner. It may also resume pumping partially while repairs continue.Saudi Arabia's government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.Saudi faces a growing supply problemThe pipeline has become vital to Saudi Arabia during the war. For the past six months, it has allowed the world's biggest oil exporter to bypass the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.Saudi Arabia has used the route to move around 4 million barrels of oil per day to Yanbu. That is roughly 4% of global oil supply.The pipeline's shutdown now threatens that alternative route.Saudi Arabia has some additional stocks at Egyptian ports. These include Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean.A fourth industry source said these stocks could supply customers for several more days.Yanbu has an estimated storage capacity of around 35 million barrels. Ain Sukhna can hold about 18 million barrels, while Sidi Kerir has capacity for around 20 million barrels.But the storage facilities are not full. The four sources said the stocks will eventually run out unless the east-west pipeline resumes operations.Saudi oil production already at 30-year lowThe latest disruption comes after a sharp fall in Saudi oil production.Saudi Arabia told OPEC that its output fell to 6.2 million barrels per day in August. That was down from 10.9 million bpd in February, before the war began.The International Energy Agency said on Friday that Saudi oil supply had fallen to its lowest level in more than three decades.It cited reduced flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.The IEA expects global oil supply to fall by 5.7 million bpd this year. That is about 6% of global supply.The Middle East supplied around 22 million bpd of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have since fallen to between 6 million and 9 million bpd, according to industry sources.The disruption has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs. It has also fuelled inflation and sent US bond yields to their highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis.More pressure on Saudi oil routesSaudi Arabia is also facing fresh risks around the Red Sea.Houthi fighters in Yemen have threatened Saudi oil shipments during the war. On Friday, they seized an island at the mouth of the Red Sea.The east-west pipeline had given Saudi Arabia a crucial way to avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Its continued shutdown could leave the kingdom increasingly dependent on stored oil and other export routes.If the pipeline takes weeks to repair, Saudi Arabia could struggle to maintain its overseas supplies.A prolonged shutdown could therefore remove millions of barrels of Saudi crude from global markets. That would further tighten supplies and add to pressure on already elevated oil prices.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1985, Andy Warhol created digital art on an Amiga computer; nearly 30 years later, researchers recovered 28 never-before-seen images from his floppy disks
articles.summary: US News: In 1985, Andy Warhol experimented with digital art on an Amiga computer as part of a commission from Commodore International. Nearly 30 years later, r.
articles.body: In 1985, Andy Warhol experimented with digital art on an Amiga computer as part of a commission from Commodore International. Nearly 30 years later, researchers recovered 28 previously unseen digital images created by the artist from floppy disks stored in the archives of The Andy Warhol Museum.The images had remained inaccessible because the files were saved in an obsolete format, according to The Andy Warhol Museum. Members of the Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) Computer Club worked with museum staff, artists and researchers to recover the data from the ageing floppy disks.Warhol, who earned a bachelor’s degree in fine arts from Carnegie Mellon University in 1949, used the Amiga to explore how his familiar artistic style could work in a new digital medium. The recovered works include experiments with Campbell’s soup cans, Botticelli’s Venus, Marilyn Monroe, a banana and portraits.The recovery project began after artist Cory Arcangel, who described himself as a "Warhol fanatic and lifelong computer nerd", learnt about Warhol’s Amiga experiments through a 1985 Commodore infomercial available on YouTube. His interest eventually led to a collaboration involving The Andy Warhol Museum, Carnegie Museum of Art, Carnegie Mellon University and the CMU Computer Club.How the forgotten files were recoveredArcangel first approached The Andy Warhol Museum in 2011 about restoring the Amiga hardware held by the museum and checking whether files could still be recovered from its associated disks. He later worked with Tina Kukielski of the Carnegie Museum of Art, who helped connect the project with Golan Levin, a CMU art professor and director of the Frank-Ratchye STUDIO for Creative Inquiry.Levin connected Arcangel with the CMU Computer Club, a student group known for its work with obsolete computer hardware and "retrocomputing". The group found that even reading the old floppy disks could put their contents at risk. The recovery therefore required unusual equipment and methods.By February 2013, the Computer Club had prepared a plan for handling the fragile disks. Members then worked with Amber Morgan, collections manager at The Andy Warhol Museum, and other archivists to try to extract the data.At first, there was no certainty that Warhol’s artwork was still present on the disks. Many of the floppy disks were system and application disks. However, the researchers discovered that Warhol had also saved his own data on them.The directory listings provided the first major clue. Files with names such as "campbells.pic" and "marilyn1.pic" suggested that images might still exist. But the excitement quickly turned into a technical problem because the files were stored in a format that available utilities could not recognise.The Computer Club’s forensics experts eventually reverse-engineered the unknown format. This allowed them to access 28 digital images that had never been seen before. Experts at The Andy Warhol Museum judged the images to be in Warhol’s style. At least 11 of the recovered images also carried Warhol’s signature.Warhol’s experiments with a new mediumThe recovered works show Warhol using digital tools to recreate subjects that were already strongly associated with his art. Campbell’s soup cans, Venus and self-portraits appear among the images.Instead of traditional painting or printing methods, the works use digital processes available through the Amiga. These include pattern flood fills, palletised colour and copy-and-paste collage.The museum said Warhol’s Amiga experiments ranged from simple doodles and photographs of a desktop to digital versions of his familiar subjects. One work from the series, a portrait of Debbie Harry, was already part of The Warhol’s collection.Cory Arcangel said, "What's amazing is that by looking at these images, we can see how quickly Warhol seemed to intuit the essence of what it meant to express oneself.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: China unveils robotic fish modelled on the golden arowana for underwater navigation
articles.summary: International News: China has showcased a highly realistic fish-shaped underwater robot that can autonomously navigate through water, highlighting the country's growing d.
articles.body: China has showcased a highly realistic fish-shaped underwater robot that can autonomously navigate through water, highlighting the country's growing development of biomimetic robotic systems with potential applications in underwater surveillance and reconnaissance.According to Chinese news outlet Jimu News, BG-5 Golden Dragon Fish, developed by Boyagongdao Marine Technology Group, was demonstrated at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing's Shougang Park. The robot is modelled on the golden arowana and uses a multi-joint tail to reproduce the swimming motion of a real fish.Jimu News quoted an exhibition staff member as saying that the robot does not follow a pre-programmed swimming route. Instead, its sensors detect obstacles and allow it to autonomously plan its movement. The report said the robot weighs 3 kg and has a three-joint tail divided into seven segments.According to the company product catalogue, the BG-5 is 640 mm long, 204 mm wide and 90 mm high, with a weight of 3 kg. It has a listed maximum operating depth of 5 metres and a maximum speed of 0.6 metres per second.The robot uses fish-tail propulsion, with its multi-joint tail generating movement through an undulating motion rather than relying on a conventional propeller. For navigation, the BG-5 is designed with autonomous obstacle-avoidance capabilities.The manufacturer also lists a BG-5V variant associated with capabilities including path planning, task allocation, formation control and multi-robot cooperation.Potential defence applicationsBoyagongdao, the developer of the BG-5, has an established defence connection in underwater robotics. The company says it has undertaken a national defence key special project involving an underwater biomimetic detection platform.It has also developed the ROBO-SHARK biomimetic underwater robot in cooperation with a military unit, according to material published by the World Robot Conference.The BG-5 fish-like form and autonomous navigation could potentially make it useful for shallow-water reconnaissance and surveillance. Its small 3-kg form factor could allow it to operate in confined or shallow underwater environments where larger unmanned underwater vehicles may be less practical. Its fish-like, multi-joint propulsion could support low-profile underwater surveillance.Its BG-5V variant with its path planning, task allocation, formation control and multi-robot coordination, potentially enabling multiple underwater robots to conduct coordinated search, surveillance and reconnaissance missions.

articles.title: Priscilla Chan helped protect a Hawaiian beach preserve and wetland habitat; 17 acres are now protected for the public
articles.summary: US News: A 17-acre stretch of coastline on Kauaʻi’s North Shore is now protected for public access and long-term conservation, with philanthropic support from .
articles.body: A 17-acre stretch of coastline on Kauaʻi’s North Shore is now protected for public access and long-term conservation, with philanthropic support from Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg helping fund its ongoing stewardship. Kāhili Beach Preserve, also known locally as Rock Quarry, includes a windswept beach, the mouth of Kīlauea Stream and important riparian areas. The Hawaiʻi Land Trust owns the preserve and holds it in perpetuity. Chan and Zuckerberg did not acquire the property themselves. Instead, their endowed gift through the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation supports the long-term care of land that was first protected through a private donation in 2003 and later expanded by HILT. The preserve now combines public beach access, habitat protection, restoration and community stewardship.How Priscilla Chan helped secure Kāhili Beach’s futurePriscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg contributed to Kāhili Beach Preserve through an endowed gift made through the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation. The Hawaiʻi Land Trust says the fund supports the preserve’s ongoing stewardship and helped establish funding for a part-time staff presence dedicated to caring for Kāhili. The contribution came after the land had already begun its conservation journey, so Chan and Zuckerberg were not the original purchasers or donors of the property. HILT’s own material says the original preserve had been protected without a dedicated stewardship fund, making long-term financial support important for its continued care. The specific value of Chan and Zuckerberg’s Kāhili gift has not been publicly disclosed in the sources available from HILT and the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation. Their contribution therefore represents support for maintaining protected land rather than the purchase of the 17-acre preserve itself.How the original beach parcel was protectedThe conservation story began in November 2003, when Louise and Monte Zweben donated a 5.43-acre oceanfront parcel to the Hawaiʻi Land Trust. The property lies at the mouth of Kīlauea Stream and beside the Kīlauea Point National Wildlife Refuge. The donation protected the shoreline while preserving public access to Kāhili Beach. The beach is also known locally as Rock Quarry and has long been used for surfing and recreation. HILT identifies public access and habitat restoration among the preserve’s main conservation values. The original donation established the foundation for protecting the coastline from future development while allowing the community to continue using the beach.How the preserve expanded to 17 acresThe protected area grew significantly a decade later. In 2013, Hawaiʻi Land Trust purchased an adjoining 12.2-acre parcel, bringing the combined Kāhili Beach Preserve to 17.63 acres. The larger property includes the Kīlauea Stream river mouth and riparian buffer areas as well as the beach and coastal landscape. HILT owns the preserve and holds it for conservation in perpetuity. The organisation's approach means the land is not simply protected temporarily but is intended to remain conserved for future generations. The expansion also increased the amount of coastal and streamside habitat that could be managed as a connected landscape rather than as a single narrow strip of beach.Why the coastline and stream habitat are importantKāhili contains several interconnected coastal environments, including sandy shoreline, dunes, the Kīlauea Stream mouth and riparian habitat. HILT highlights the importance of the area's muliwai, where freshwater from the stream meets the ocean. These transition zones can provide important habitat and feeding opportunities for coastal wildlife. The preserve also supports native coastal vegetation, while the nearby Kīlauea Point National Wildlife Refuge adds another layer of protected habitat to the surrounding landscape. HILT's conservation work at Kāhili includes addressing invasive plants, marine debris and erosion. Protecting the land therefore helps preserve more than recreational beach access. It also maintains a section of the coastal ecosystem where freshwater, terrestrial and marine environments meet.How the community is helping care for the preserveKāhili’s conservation story has continued through local volunteer work and restoration. After the original 2003 donation, Hawaiʻi Land Trust worked with the Kīlauea Neighborhood Association on regular beach clean-ups. HILT says volunteers have contributed more than 1,000 person-hours to such efforts. More recent activities have included removing invasive vegetation and planting native coastal species. The trust also organises educational programmes and guided Talk Story on the Land experiences, giving visitors an opportunity to learn about the area's native plants, wildlife and cultural history. Together, land protection, philanthropic stewardship and community involvement have helped turn Kāhili into more than a protected parcel. The 17.63-acre preserve now provides public access while giving a coastal ecosystem a long-term layer of protection.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Japan nuclear operator chief to quit after quake data scandal, reactor restart plans hit
articles.summary: Rest of World News: The president of Chubu Electric Power is set to step down after a scandal involving manipulated earthquake data at its Hamaoka nuclear plant, Japanese.
articles.body: The president of Chubu Electric Power is set to step down after a scandal involving manipulated earthquake data at its Hamaoka nuclear plant, Japanese media reported on Monday. The company is also expected to abandon plans to restart two reactors at the facility.President Kingo Hayashi and chairman Satoru Katsuno will resign, according to public broadcaster NHK and other local media. Chubu Electric is expected to hold a press conference later on Monday. The company was not immediately available for comment.The Hamaoka plant is in central Japan, near a seismic fault line and an area considered vulnerable to a major earthquake. It has been undergoing regulatory safety checks as Chubu Electric seeks approval to restart two reactors.Data scandal puts restart plans at riskIn January, the operator admitted that it had submitted data to regulators that underestimated the earthquake risks facing the plant. The Nuclear Regulation Authority suspended its safety review process for Hamaoka in late December.A 250-page report by an independent panel, released on Monday, said management pressure contributed to the misconduct. It said the management’s "reprimand" over delays in the restart review had placed pressure on employees and was "one of the factors contributing to the misconduct".The Nikkei business daily reported that Chubu Electric would withdraw its application for the safety review.The estimate of maximum seismic ground motion is a key factor in designing nuclear plants to withstand earthquakes. In September 2023, the NRA approved Chubu Electric’s estimate of 1,200 gal, a unit used to measure ground acceleration during an earthquake.However, the regulator received information from a whistleblower in February last year about possible data fraud.Japan seeks to revive nuclear powerThe Hamaoka plant is located in Omaezaki, in Shizuoka prefecture, close to the expected route of a major Pacific earthquake. In 2024, the Japan Meteorological Agency issued its first special advisory over the possibility of a "megaquake" in the Nankai Trough area. The advisory was lifted a week later.Japan largely abandoned nuclear power after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami caused reactors at the Fukushima Daiichi plant to melt down. The country is now seeking to restart nuclear facilities to reduce its dependence on imported fossil fuels, meet rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.The world’s largest nuclear power plant, Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, resumed operations earlier this year.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1974, two siblings released their cattle before leaving a Scottish island; 50 years later, the herd showed wild deer-like social behaviour and defeated bulls lived on a separate headland
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover the fascinating story of how a herd of cattle on Swona Island adapted to life without human intervention, evolving into a distinct breed over 50 years.
articles.body: Swona was once home to a small farming and fishing community that gradually disappeared as its residents grew older and left the island. After their owners departed, only a few of the remaining animals managed to survive on their own. However, a small herd of cattle on a little island in the Pentland Firth did just that and has been flourishing for more than 50 years, mostly unaffected by human activity. The island, known as Swona, lies in the Pentland Firth between Orkney and mainland Scotland. Since its last inhabitants departed in 1974, Swona has become a case study for scientists interested in the behaviour of domestic animals when they are completely released from human control.In a rush, left behindBy the early 1970s, Swona's population had been declining for decades, and by 1974, just two people lived there: an old brother and sister named James and Violet Rosie. The Swona Heritage notes that intensive husbandry ended when the Rosies left the island in 1974. One stormy night in March James felt dangerously ill, and Violet sent for the lifeboat. She urged the crew to assist her and let free the tiny herd when they were leaving, not knowing whether they would ever return, rather than leaving the animals shut in with no one to feed them. The herd consisted of eight cows and one bull, with the cattle derived from Shorthorn and Aberdeen Angus stock.The following year, an attempt was made to bring the cattle back to the mainland, but Swona had no good harbour, just a rocky landing that was unsuitable in poor weather. The roundup went horribly. A couple of animals broke their legs during handling and were euthanised afterwards. Then no one tried again. The herd was left on the island with no regular husbandry, but additional hay was supplied for a few years, with the last winter feeding recorded in 1977.A herd that followed its own rulesWhat happened next startled practically everyone who looked at it. Thus isolated from any outside breeding stock, the cattle developed a closed, self-sustaining community and increased steadily, from nine to more than thirty animals in a decade or so. In difficult times they would eat seaweed, and when the winter storms came round Orkney, they would take shelter in the damaged crofts.Their social behaviour was also modified. Unlike the loose grazing pattern typical of a farmed herd, the Swona cattle started to impose a more wild ungulate-like organisation on themselves, like red deer. Bulls fight for control within the group, and the loser is forced to a different headland at the north end of the island, living apart from the main herd until it can fight its way back in or simply living out its remaining years in solitude. Cows, however, seem to stay with the herd for life and seem to raise their calves communally rather than in separate family groups. After decades without controlled breeding, the Swona herd has developed distinctive characteristics and is listed as a distinct breed in the World Dictionary of Livestock Breeds.Why scientists continue to observeThe Swona herd is one of only a few truly feral groups of Bos taurus, the domestic cow species, anywhere in the globe. Its rarity gives it value to researchers examining how quickly a domesticated animal reverts to wild patterns of behaviour when human supervision is completely removed. Research has studied the herd's population, its social structure and even how individual animals age and die without medical care as far back as the 1980s. It is a protected-status island, yet the cattle are pretty much left to their own devices. Swona is privately owned and hard to reach, which has helped preserve the herd's seclusion.Half a century after the Rosies left, the island is an unintentional experiment in what happens when farm animals are just left to be something else. No one had gone to Swona to breed a new breed of cattle. It happened because two old islanders had little choice but to open a gate and let the animals take it from there.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2025, Skagit County bought development rights on four Washington farms totalling 270 acres, permanently protecting prime soil as housing pressure grows
articles.summary: US News: In a strategic move to combat housing pressures, Skagit County has successfully preserved 270 acres of prime agricultural land in 2025 through its Farmland Legacy Programme, ensuring the protection of irreplaceable soil and maintaining the region's agricultural heritage.
articles.body: Land on the outskirts of expanding towns and communities in the United States is constantly under pressure to change from being agricultural. The soil quality that took centuries to develop is permanently lost if a field is paved over for a warehouse or divided for homes. The agriculture corridor along Interstate 5 in northwest Washington, where some of the nation's most productive soil is located within commuting distance of Seattle, is one of the few locations that best exemplifies the conflict between growth and food production. For almost thirty years, one county in that corridor has discreetly bought its way out of that pattern, one farm at a time.Exchanging a promise for a rewardIn 2025, Skagit County's Farmland Legacy Program protected four properties in Bow and Mount Vernon, adding 270 acres of prime farmland to the land permanently protected from residential development. The properties covered 40 and 83 acres in Bow and 40 and 107 acres in Mount Vernon, and all were designated by the US Department of Agriculture as prime farmland. A total of 585,000 dollars was paid to the four families involved under the scheme in return for giving up the right to ever build dwellings on the site.The agreement is made through what's called a conservation easement. Rather than purchasing the land, the county pays farmers for the development rights associated with it. This legal action permanently limits the site to agriculture, regardless of future ownership. Families can still farm their land, sell it or pass it on, but the easement runs with the property forever, eliminating the possibility to cash out to a housing developer. The scheme, which began in 1997, has already conserved about 15,400 acres of Skagit agriculture.Four families, four causesThe 2025 additions were from the Roozen, Nelson, Peth and Houser families, each with a long history of farming in the region. Jerry Nelson, a third-generation Skagit farmer and proprietor of Double N Potatoes, placed an easement on 40 acres near the Skagit Regional Airport. Including land protected through earlier easements, the Nelson family has now placed about 1,500 acres of Skagit farmland under the program, the most of any participant. Nelson said the relinquishment of development rights helps offset the cost of holding the site and is a basic choice not to see the area developed. He also said that dwellings across farmland made the remaining fields tougher to reach, since heavy machinery and irrigation systems did not work well alongside residential properties.The Houser family, which has farmed in the Sedro-Woolley area for generations, placed a conservation easement on 107 acres near the intersection of McLean and LaConner Whitney roads, while father-son pair Dan and Owen Peth protected more than 80 acres of their cattle ranch. Each family sacrificed a significant amount of money they could have made by selling to a developer, choosing continuity on the land over greater payment.Racing against a statewide trendSkagit's approach stands out because it runs directly against the wider pattern across Washington. American Farmland Trust's Farms Under Threat analysis found that Washington lost nearly 98,000 acres of farmland between 2001 and 2019, while the state's 2022 Census of Agriculture recorded a 5.2% decline in farmland. The group figures that somewhere in the country, people are converting about 2,000 acres of farmland to urban or low-density residential usage every single day, nationally.Skagit County's 2025 result came below its longer-term target of protecting an average of 400 acres a year for the next 25 years. The county had protected 460 acres in 2024, compared with 270 acres in 2025, but the annual figures are only part of a broader effort that has now placed about 15,400 acres under permanent protection. The program works through voluntary conservation easements, meaning landowners choose to give up development rights while retaining ownership and continuing to farm the property. The program's continued expansion depended not only on county funding and long-term targets but also on farmers choosing to preserve their land rather than sell its development rights.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
